<!-- fak-crossaudit-key: crossaudit-router-v1 -->

## Parent context

Part of #3846. This is one dispatchable leaf in the independent cross-model issue-audit program.

## Current state

Account routing resolves a configured model but review flags do not select an auditor from author provenance or enforce a diversified fallback chain.

## Why this is next

The user's desired Claude-versus-GPT/open-weight reciprocal audit must be a policy-driven route, not an operator remembering which flag to pass.

## Working spine

`PlanIssueAudit(author,risk,roster,health)` returns a priced ordered auditor plan plus the independence proof for each candidate.

## Priority context

Depends on the identity policy and spine; blocks unattended loops.

## In scope

Declarative reciprocal rules for Claude, GPT/Codex, and local/open-weight authors; risk-tier provider-diversity requirements; reasoning effort; model-tier floor; health/capacity checks; ordered fallback; unknown-author quorum; cost estimate; no-independent-auditor refusal.

## Out of scope

No background scheduler, live credential refresh, hard-coded unreleased model availability, or verdict aggregation beyond plan construction.

## Done condition

Table tests prove Claude->configured GPT/local, GPT->Claude/local, local->frontier, unknown->diversified quorum, same-family alias skipped, unhealthy provider skipped, and no valid route returns a typed refusal.

## Witness

`go test ./internal/modelroute -run TestPlanIssueAudit` with fixtures for GPT xhigh, Claude, and a local open-weight target; emitted plan includes identity and independence reasons.

## Acceptance gate

`fak buildcheck --vet ./internal/modelroute` and all audit routing matrix tests pass.

## Dependencies

Blocked by #3847
Blocked by #3848

## Closure binding

Closing commit references this issue and carries `(fak modelroute)`; route output attached to #3846 contains no credential values.

## Work unit

leaf

7

## Scale

S1

## Required model tier

tier/T1-required

## Optimal model tier

tier/T0-optimal

## Assumptions

- Provider health/account readiness can be read through existing modelroute seams.
- Specific IDs such as gpt-5.6-sol and effort xhigh are operator roster/config data, not hard-coded product constants.

## Confusion risks

- Falling back from GPT to a different alias of the same family.
- Selecting a cheap local auditor whose capability tier is below the issue risk without surfacing the downgrade.

## Coordination

- Modelroute leaf; reuse account readiness and model-tier metadata, and do not add secrets to routing manifests.

## Trigger

Operator request on 2026-07-10 to create independent cross-model background audits for general issue work and silent/adversarial/model-specific corruption.

## Batch policy

One issue per fak-crossaudit marker key; reruns update an existing open or closed issue instead of creating a duplicate; the producer scans at most 500 issues per planning run.
